claim: test_hashing.md S9 ("Project requirement leaf hash is invariant under derivation graduation") asserts that given three spec fixtures identical except for one project requirement's `derivation` field (absent / `"pending"` / removed again), 'the root hashes of all three trees are identical.' arch_tree_builder.md's Tree Structure table (row `meta/project`) defines that leaf as hashed 'from the bytes of project.json' — the literal file bytes, not a field-level serialization like requirement leaves get — and this row is unchanged by the derivation-status epic's edit to this same file (only the Requirement Leaf Hashing section's allowlist prose changed).
authoritative_source: arch_tree_builder.md's own Tree Structure table is the authoritative, unmodified definition of the meta/project leaf: raw bytes of project.json. That rule predates this epic and is deliberate — it is how validate/diff notice any textual change to the project envelope, not just requirement-field edits.
evidence: Root hash = HashChildren over [meta/project leaf, project requirement leaves, module hashes] (arch_tree_builder.md "Tree Structure" + flow_hash_computation.md). meta/project's hash is SHA-256 of project.json's literal bytes (HashFile), independent of any per-field allowlist. Adding `"derivation": "pending"` to a requirement object inside project.json necessarily changes the file's byte content, so the meta/project leaf hash necessarily changes between the 'no derivation' and 'pending' fixture variants, even though the requirement leaf itself correctly stays invariant (its hash comes from the allowlisted JSON serialization that already omits `derivation` in the current, unchanged `hashRequirement` implementation in merkle/tree_builder.go). A changed meta/project leaf flows straight into a changed root hash by construction, so S9's root-hash assertion cannot hold for the 'pending' variant against the other two — this is a mathematical consequence of hashing project.json's raw bytes for the envelope leaf, a rule this very spec leaf establishes and that this epic left untouched, not an implementation bug. I confirmed this empirically: implementing S9 literally (the requirement-leaf allowlist already matches spec) reproduces a matching requirement-leaf hash but a mismatched root hash for the 'pending' tree. The contradiction also defeats this epic's stated design goal beyond the test itself: ImpactClassifier (425146f32e96) classifies a changed project.json meta leaf as `structural` impact regardless of which field inside it changed, so even with the requirement leaf correctly invariant, `spex diff` still reports a `meta/project` modification and `spex plan` still mints a structural change on derivation graduation — directly contradicting arch_tree_builder.md's own rationale that 'graduating a requirement from pending to derived must produce no content change — no diff entry, no impact, no absorb entry to write.' Two of my four spec leaves for this bead (arch_tree_builder.md, test_hashing.md) are therefore mutually unsatisfiable as written, and I have no basis to decide which one yields.
proposed_fix: Pick one, in the authoring loop: (a) narrow S9 to assert only the requirement leaf's own hash invariance and drop the root-hash assertion, accepting that project.json's raw-bytes meta leaf will still show a diff/structural-impact entry on any textual edit including derivation graduation — meaning the 'no diff entry, no impact' promise in the Requirement Leaf Hashing rationale needs to be walked back to 'no *requirement-leaf* content change', or handled downstream (e.g. a diff/impact special case that ignores a meta/project change whose only effect is a derivation-field edit); or (b) change how meta/project is hashed — from raw file bytes to the same derivation-excluding field-level serialization already used for the project's requirements array — which would make root invariance achievable but is a materially bigger behavior change (it loses the 'catch any textual/formatting change in project.json' property the raw-bytes rule exists for, per the flow doc's framing of meta leaves as envelope-level guards). This implementer cannot choose between narrowing a test guarantee and changing a hashing rule that both of my spec leaves currently describe as settled.
